clue.text: This part of the body turns me sick

indicators.note: something sick is out of sorts, so the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a certain part of their body makes them feel nauseous.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is a bone in the chest, so it is a part of the body.

clue.text: Racetrack tout's gratuity half in sterling

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, so the rest is dropped

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity
the British currency, of which only the front half survives

explanation.surface: A racecourse tout is paid a small tip in British pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells predictions about races, which is what a racetrack tout does.

clue.text: Light working fabric

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: A lightweight material suitable for working clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light working' looks like a description of the fabric, but each word gives a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile made from cellulose, a man-made fabric.

clue.text: Rebuke for terrible pub attack

indicators.note: terrible suggests something in a sorry state, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for an awful assault on a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold or reprimand them, a synonym of rebuke.

clue.text: Emotionally hardened state with warped soul

parts.note: an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: a warped thing is bent out of shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A person whose soul has become twisted is described as emotionally hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A callous person has grown insensitive and unfeeling, the hardened state the clue describes.

clue.text: Foreigners on a Nile cruise to the south

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a cruise wanders about, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Tourists from abroad sail down the Nile towards the south of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are people from another country, the legal sense of foreigners.

clue.text: Gambling games: Tories let fly

indicators.note: letting the letters fly scatters them, so they land in a new order

parts.note: both words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians loosen the rules on gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotteries are games of chance in which numbered tickets are drawn for prizes, a form of gambling.

clue.text: Peacekeepers genteel? Not at all

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
civil means polite, well-mannered

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether UN peacekeepers are refined and concludes they are not.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: peacekeepers who are anything but genteel would be rude, and the pieces spell that out.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncivil means rude and discourteous, the opposite of polite and refined.

clue.text: Stop Paris and Rome, for example, being written in large plain lettering

parts.note: to block is to stop
Paris and Rome are each the capital city of a country

explanation.surface: Instructions to halt travel to two European cities are written in big letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Block capitals are simple, separate upper-case letters, as asked for on official forms.

clue.text: Lively son to ask personal questions

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to pry is to be nosy about private matters

explanation.surface: A lively boy is busy being nosy with his questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, often older, who is active and nimble, a synonym of lively.

clue.text: Still basic new study of trajectories

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters form a fresh arrangement

parts.note: both words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a fresh field of research into trajectories is still rather elementary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistics is the science of the flight of projectiles such as bullets and shells, the paths they follow.

clue.text: South Africa includes thanks to New Zealand as part of a poem

indicators.note: something that includes other things holds them inside itself

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for South Africa
ta is informal British for thank you
the standard abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: A poem's section expresses South Africa's gratitude to New Zealand, perhaps after a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a verse, a group of lines forming one unit of a poem.

clue.text: Imagine criminal with dreadful vice at some point

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad way, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Picture a lawbreaker who has some terrible vice at some moment in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At some point' sounds like 'at some time', but it means a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceive of something is to form it in the mind, to imagine it.

clue.text: Tricky pedicure involving judge showing bias

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other
something tricky is awkward or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A difficult foot treatment given to a judge reveals partiality.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice is a preconceived opinion favouring or opposing something, which is bias.

clue.text: Jack's universal tax problem? Pretend to sit side by side

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: a problem is something gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal
taken as written for rearranging
to pose is to pretend

explanation.surface: Jack has a tax problem that applies to everyone and fakes sitting beside someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To juxtapose things is to place them next to each other, for comparison or contrast.

clue.text: Sort of fiddle with a plant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stringed instrument a little larger than a violin
second meaning: a flowering plant genus that includes pansies and violets

explanation.surface: Someone tinkers with a plant, a gardener's fiddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle with' reads as a verb meaning tinker, but 'fiddle' is the noun for a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is a member of the violin family, and the pansy and violet belong to the botanical genus of that name.

clue.text: Authorised agent to make enquiries about animal

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to pry is to inquire nosily
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A representative is sent to investigate a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a person given authority to act or vote on another's behalf.

clue.text: Satisfied salesman's permitted to take note

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
let means allowed
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A contented salesman has been allowed to write something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full up, satisfied after eating plenty.

clue.text: Period in which terrible storm affected athlete

indicators.note: a period in which things happen holds them inside it

parts.note: a span is a stretch of time

indicators.note: terrible means in a bad state, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An athlete's performance was hampered by a spell of bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman is a man who plays sports, so an athlete is a fair example.

clue.text: Desired building once lived in

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are assembled in a new way

parts.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a coveted building where they used to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as a noun, a house, but it is a verb telling you to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell somewhere; in the past tense, resided means lived in a place at an earlier time.

clue.text: Inept article on mother's true, unfortunately!

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone sadly admits that a piece written about their mother being clumsy is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur as an adjective means unskilled or unprofessional, hence inept.

clue.text: Splendid way to get the best

parts.note: fine means excellent, splendid
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An excellent method for obtaining top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The finest is the superlative of fine, the very best of a kind.

clue.text: Here is a trap I designed for a beekeeper

indicators.note: something designed is planned and constructed, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: the words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a trap they have built for catching a beekeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist keeps bees, from Latin apis meaning bee, the formal word for a beekeeper.

clue.text: Flash dash!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to run naked through a public place
second meaning: to move very fast

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs: one is exposing oneself in public, the other is rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is both to run naked in public, exposing oneself, and to move at great speed.

clue.text: River with unusual lure for monarch

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An angler uses a strange bait on a river, fishing for a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign who reigns over a country, a kind of ruler.

clue.text: It's about mannequin going first to get changed

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a mannequin is a dummy model used to display clothes
someone who led was going first, in front

explanation.surface: A shop dummy is first in line to have its outfit swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Remodelled means reshaped or reworked, that is, changed in form.

clue.text: Vegetable found in Staffordshire?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a market town in Staffordshire, a county in the English Midlands

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second meaning is a place name rather than a definition proper: Leek is a market town in Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is a long onion relative and a national emblem of Wales; the place is a town in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Under a mountain in Scotland with topsoil but no river

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: but no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: earth is the soil on the ground
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Something lies below a Scottish peak that has soil on top but no stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath is a preposition meaning below, the same sense as under.

clue.text: Fans love to run on Sunday

parts.note: to adore is to love
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
S is an abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Enthusiasts enjoy going for a jog at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorers are people who worship or admire something, as fans do.
